info.name: VCST-5933 — organizationOrders authorizes on raw membership (self-contained)
info.description:
Self-contained reproducible evidence for VCST-5933. Locks and unlocks the membership over the REST API, so no seeder script is needed.

LAST RUN 2026-09-09 via newman: 13/13 requests, 23 assertions, 1 failed — request 8, which is the evidence. Teardown verified back to V1.

THE DEFECT: organizationOrders(organizationId:) authorizes through CanAccessOrderAuthorizationHandler -> IsCustomerOrganization -> Contact.Organizations.Contains(organizationId) — raw membership, never lock-aware. organization(id:) re-evaluates the lock. The two reads disagree for a member who is LOCKED OUT.

THE ORDER IS NOT ARBITRARY — two measured facts force it:
 1. Platform REST needs a CONTEXT-FREE ADMIN token. A storefront-scoped token gets 401 invalid_token, so lock/unlock cannot reuse the buyer's (requests 1-4 and 12-13 use the admin token).
 2. A V2 lock KILLS a token minted BEFORE it. So the buyer authenticates at request 5, AFTER the lock.

WHY EVERY CONTROL IS HERE — no single request carries the finding:
 · request 8 (THE DEFECT) is meaningless without 7: same principal, same org, refused
 · 9 proves the refusal is LOCK-specific, not a blanket customer-principal denial
 · 10 proves the query really reads the named org (measured 66 vs 14)
 · 11 proves it is not simply ungated — a NON-MEMBER org IS refused
 · 5 proves the buyer token is scoped to the UNLOCKED org, so nothing request 8 returns about the locked org can be explained by the token's scope

READ-BACK IS MANDATORY: POST .../{id}/lock on an unknown membership id returns 200 with a null body, NOT 404. Request 4 verifies the state instead of trusting request 3's status; request 13 does the same for the unlock.

DO NOT RUN WITH --bail. Requests 12-13 unlock the fixture; --bail would stop at request 8 and leave it LOCKED, poisoning suites 006 and 050d.

GRAPHQL BODIES USE mode:"graphql", never raw (qa-postman SKILL.md Rules).

RUN: newman run <collection> -e <env> --env-var "adminUser=$ADMIN" --env-var "adminPassword=$ADMIN_PASSWORD_VCST" --env-var "b2bUserPassword=$DEFAULT_TEST_PASSWORD"

request.description: Context-free admin grant — no storeId, no organization_id. Only this token may call /api/customer/**; a storefront-scoped token returns 401 invalid_token.

item.name: 2. SETUP — find the membership id (discovered, not hardcoded)

exec: pm.test('exactly one membership for (user, locked org)', () => pm.expect(r.length, 'results').to.equal(1));
console.log('membership id:', r[0].id, '| isCurrentlyLocked before:', r[0].isCurrentlyLocked);

request.description: Discovered, not hardcoded: membership ids are platform-assigned and change on every re-seed. The search REQUIRES a scoping filter (UserId/OrganizationId) or returns BadRequest. Genuine REST JSON, so mode:raw is correct here.

item.name: 3. SETUP — LOCK the membership (V2: permanent, non-active org)

exec: // A 200 proves nothing: lock on an UNKNOWN id also returns 200 with a null body, not 404.
pm.test('lock call accepted (status only — not proof)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 204]));

request.description: Empty body = permanent lock (no lockoutEnd), the V2 state. An atomic timed lock would pass lockoutEnd here.

item.name: 4. SETUP — READ BACK and prove it is locked

exec: pm.test('READ-BACK: membership is now currently locked', () => {
console.log('locked:', m.isLocked, '| currentlyLocked:', m.isCurrentlyLocked, '| lockoutEnd:', m.lockoutEnd);

request.description: The real precondition gate. Without it a silently-failed lock leaves every downstream request returning 200 and the run passes while proving nothing.

item.name: 5. Buyer auth — AFTER the lock, and with NO organization_id

exec: console.log('organization_id claim on the buyer token:', payload.organization_id || '(none)');
// The grant sends NO organization_id, but BL-AUTH-015 step 5 still resolves 'the first
// ACCESSIBLE organization' — so the claim is the UNLOCKED org, not absent. Measured 2026-09-09.
// That is a STRONGER control than an absent claim: the token is scoped to the UNLOCKED org, so
// anything request 8 returns about the LOCKED org cannot be explained by the token's scope, and
// cannot be the BL-AUTH-016 fallback either — a fallback would have had to be ASKED for the
// locked org, and this grant never names one.
pm.test('the buyer token is NOT scoped to the locked org — so nothing below can be explained by its scope', () => {
pm.test('the token resolved to the unlocked org (BL-AUTH-015 step 5: first accessible org)', () => {

request.description: MUST come after the lock — a V2 lock revokes tokens minted before it. storeId is camelCase-only; omitting it returns 400 user_cannot_login_in_store on valid credentials, masking the org error.

exec: pm.test('200, no GraphQL errors', () => { pm.response.to.have.status(200); pm.expect(pm.response.json().errors, 'errors[]').to.be.undefined; });
pm.test('the buyer sees the locked org flagged, and the control org not flagged', () => {
if (!nm) { console.log('nonMemberOrgId unset — request 11 will SKIP, stated not silently passed.'); pm.collectionVariables.set('nonMemberUsable', 'false'); }

else { pm.test('nonMemberOrgId is genuinely NOT a membership of this caller', () => pm.expect(d.organizationsIds || [], 'organizationsIds').to.not.include(nm)); pm.collectionVariables.set('nonMemberUsable', 'true'); }

graphql.query: query { me { contact { organizationsIds organizations(first: 50) { totalCount items { id name isLockedForCurrentUser } } } } }

request.description: Confirms the lock is visible to the buyer's own principal, and re-verifies the non-member control rather than trusting the environment note.

item.name: 7. CONTROL A — organization(id: locked) is REFUSED

exec: pm.test('HTTP 200 (GraphQL reports errors inside a 200)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('organization(id: locked) is Forbidden and returns no data', () => {

request.description: The reference behaviour: this read DOES re-evaluate the lock.

item.name: 8. THE DEFECT — organizationOrders(locked) must agree with request 7

exec: console.log('  ...while the buyer token is scoped to', pm.collectionVariables.get('tokenOrgClaim'), '(the UNLOCKED org)');
// ASSERTS THE CORRECT EXPECTATION, NOT THE MEASURED BEHAVIOUR.
// Two org-scoped reads of the SAME org id by the SAME principal must agree on accessibility.
// FAILS while VCST-5933 is open — that failure IS the evidence. Goes green on the fix.
// Deliberately does NOT assert that order history must be hidden: which read is wrong is a
// product decision QA does not make here.
pm.test('VCST-5933: organizationOrders must agree with organization(id:) for the same locked org', () => {
pm.expect(refused, 'organizationOrders refused the locked org, as organization(id:) did').to.equal(true);

graphql.query: query($orgId: String!) { organizationOrders(organizationId: $orgId, first: 5) { totalCount items { id number status } } }

request.description: Measured 2026-09-09: 200 with totalCount 66 — the LOCKED org's full order history, returned to a buyer holding a token scoped to the UNLOCKED org. So the query ignores both the lock and the token's org scope.

item.name: 9. CONTROL B — organization(id: unlocked) is SERVED

exec: pm.test('organization(id: unlocked) returns data — so request 7 was not a blanket denial', () => {

request.description: Without this, request 7's Forbidden could just mean a storefront customer principal may never read organization(id:).

item.name: 10. CONTROL C — organizationOrders(unlocked) returns a DIFFERENT count

exec: console.log('locked totalCount =', l, '| unlocked totalCount =', u);
if (l !== 'null') { pm.test('the two orgs return DIFFERENT counts — request 8 really read the named org', () => pm.expect(String(u), 'unlocked vs locked').to.not.equal(l)); }
else { console.log('request 8 was refused, so no count to discriminate against — expected once fixed.'); }

graphql.query: query($orgId: String!) { organizationOrders(organizationId: $orgId, first: 5) { totalCount items { id number status } } }

request.description: Measured 2026-09-09: totalCount 14, against 66 for the locked org. Different counts prove the organizationId argument is honoured.

item.name: 11. CONTROL D — organizationOrders(NON-MEMBER org) IS refused

// The finding depends on this: the query is not simply ungated. It gates on MEMBERSHIP
pm.test('a NON-MEMBER org IS refused — so organizationOrders gates on membership, not nothing', () => {

request.description: Pins the defect precisely. Without it the report could only say organizationOrders is unauthorized, which is false and would send the fix in the wrong direction.

exec: pm.test('unlock call accepted (status only — request 13 is the proof)', () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([200, 204]));

request.description: Runs even when request 8 fails — Newman does not stop on a failed assertion unless --bail is passed. Do NOT pass --bail, or the fixture is left LOCKED.

item.name: 13. CLEANUP — READ BACK and prove the fixture is at rest (V1)

exec: pm.test('TEARDOWN VERIFIED: membership is back to unlocked (V1)', () => {
console.log('final state — isLocked:', m.isLocked, '| isCurrentlyLocked:', m.isCurrentlyLocked);

request.description: A teardown that is not verified is not a teardown. Leaving this fixture locked would poison suite 006, 050d and anything else authenticating as this account.
